surface_mechanism_description: The surface mechanism involves the initial interaction of TMI with surface P-dimers, resulting in a change in anisotropy. At higher temperatures, the introduction of TMI leads to a steady increase in RA response, suggesting the decomposition of TMI at P-dimers, creating In-dimers that react with incoming phosphine molecules to return the surface to the starting condition.
evidence: The text describes that the introduction of TMI leads to a change in anisotropy and that at higher temperatures, the decomposition of TMI at P-dimers creates In-dimers, which then react with incoming phosphine molecules. It also mentions that a residual species such as monomethylindium may act as a site blocking agent.
